articles.content_html:
The Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB) have issued the official examination notice for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) 2026 Computer Based Test 1 (CBT-1). Published on September 15, 2026, the notification outlines critical operational guidelines and exam timeline updates for engineering and technical diploma candidates nationwide. Candidates must track official announcements strictly through the central board domain at rrbcdg.gov.in.

Key Highlights & Important Dates

Event / Activity Official Date / Status
Notification ReleasedSeptember 15, 2026
Official Exam ScheduleAnnounced for 2026
Official Portalrrbcdg.gov.in

Overview & Background of Railway Recruitment Boards Notification

The Railway Recruitment Boards operate under the Ministry of Railways to execute large-scale technical recruitments across all Indian Railway zones. The Assistant Loco Pilot recruitment represents one of the premier technical entry-level cadres in the Indian Railways operational system. Assistant Loco Pilots work alongside Senior Loco Pilots to ensure safe, efficient, and timely train operations across freight and passenger networks.

The central recruitment update released on September 15, 2026, officially activates the timeline for the Computer Based Test (CBT-1). CBT-1 functions as the mandatory preliminary screening stage for all registered applicants. While total vacancy distributions are defined under official notification guidelines across participating zonal RRBs, performance in CBT-1 directly determines candidate progression to subsequent specialized selection rounds.

Eligibility Criteria & Minimum Educational Qualifications

Candidates applying for the Assistant Loco Pilot post must fulfill prescribed technical educational qualifications prior to the closing date of applications. General academic degrees without technical specialization are not eligible for this position.

  • Matriculation Plus ITI: SSLC/Matriculation combined with an ITI certificate from recognized NCVT/SCVT institutions in trades such as Fitter, Electrician, Instrument Mechanic, Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic, Mechanic Radio & TV, Electronics Mechanic, Wireman, Armature & Coil Winder, Tractor Mechanic, Auto Electrician, or Motor Vehicle Mechanic.
  • Diploma in Engineering: Three-year Diploma in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics, or Automobile Engineering from a recognized technical board or institution.
  • Degree in Engineering: Combination of engineering disciplines or a Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering (B.E./B.Tech) in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics, or Automobile streams from a recognized university.

Age Limit Criteria & Category-Wise Relaxations

Applicants must fall within the prescribed age bracket as defined under official recruitment rules. The standard minimum age limit is 18 years, with an upper age limit generally capped at 30 years as of the designated cut-off date specified in the central notification.

Upper age relaxations apply strictly to candidates belonging to reserved categories under Government of India guidelines:

  • Other Backward Classes (OBC Non-Creamy Layer): 3 years relaxation above the upper age limit.
  • Scheduled Castes (SC) & Scheduled Tribes (ST): 5 years relaxation above the upper age limit.
  • Ex-Servicemen (ESM): Relaxation equivalent to the length of service rendered in armed forces plus 3 years, subject to central rules.
  • Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD): Applicable strictly as per job role suitability specified in the official notice.

Pay Scale, Salary Structure & 7th CPC Allowances

Selected candidates are appointed to Level-2 of the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) Pay Matrix. The initial basic pay for an Assistant Loco Pilot is fixed at ₹19,900 per month, supplemented by standard central government allowances.

Pay ElementDetails & Terms
Basic Pay₹19,900 per month (Level-2, 7th CPC)
Dearness Allowance (DA)Calculated on basic pay as per prevailing central rates
House Rent Allowance (HRA)Varies by city classification (X, Y, Z categories)
Running AllowanceSpecial mileage allowance based on actual distance operated
Transport & MedicalStandard Transport Allowance (TA) and free railway medical care

With running allowances added after operational training, gross monthly earnings increase substantially, providing strong long-term career progression into Senior Loco Pilot, Power Controller, and Loco Inspector roles.

Comprehensive Examination Pattern & Syllabus Structure

The CBT-1 examination is a screening test designed to assess fundamental numerical ability, logical reasoning, scientific awareness, and current affairs knowledge. The test comprises 75 objective multiple-choice questions (MCQs) to be completed within a duration of 60 minutes.

  • Mathematics (20 Questions): Number system, BODMAS, Decimals, Fractions, LCM/HCF, Ratio and Proportion, Percentages, Mensuration, Time and Work, Time and Distance, Simple and Compound Interest, Profit and Loss, Algebra, Geometry, and Trigonometry.
  • Mental Ability / Reasoning (25 Questions): Analogies, Alphabetical and Number Series, Coding and Decoding, Mathematical Operations, Relationships, Syllogism, Jumbling, Venn Diagrams, Data Interpretation, and Direction Sense.
  • General Science (20 Questions): Physics, Chemistry, and Life Sciences covering standard 10th-grade (CBSE/NCERT) curricula.
  • General Awareness (10 Questions): Current affairs, technology, sports, culture, personalities, economics, and politics.

Negative marking is enforced across all test sessions. One-third (1/3rd) of the marks assigned to a question will be deducted for every incorrect response. Normalization of marks is applied when tests are administered across multiple shifts.

Step-by-Step Online Application & Document Upload Guide

Applicants must complete their administrative requirements through the official recruitment portals. Follow these instructions to view notices and complete official verification procedures:

  1. Navigate directly to the official portal of Railway Recruitment Boards at rrbcdg.gov.in.
  2. Locate the latest announcements section on the homepage.
  3. Click on the specific notice link titled RRB ALP 2026 Assistant Loco Pilot Computer Based Test (CBT-1) Exam Dates Announced (or open https://rrbcdg.gov.in/notices/cen-alp-2026-cbt1-schedule.pdf).
  4. Download the official PDF document to review exam schedule dates, shift instructions, and reporting requirements.
  5. Ensure personal details, uploaded photograph, scanned signature, and category certificates align with the instructions specified in the notification.

Selection Stages & Final Merit List Formulation

The recruitment of Assistant Loco Pilots follows a rigorous multi-stage qualification framework to ensure candidates meet strict technical and medical standards:

  • Stage 1 - CBT 1: Preliminary screening test. Marks scored are normalized and used solely to shortlist candidates for CBT-2.
  • Stage 2 - CBT 2: Divided into Part A (Maths, Reasoning, Basic Science & Engineering) which forms the basis for shortlisting to CBAT, and Part B (Trade Test) which is qualifying in nature (minimum 35% pass mark required for all categories).
  • Stage 3 - Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT): Specialized psychological test evaluating spatial memory, depth perception, and reaction speed. Candidates must score a minimum cutoff (T-score of 42) in each test battery.
  • Stage 4 - Document Verification (DV) & Medical Examination: Candidates who qualify CBAT undergo document verification followed by a comprehensive medical evaluation. Candidates must pass the strict A-1 Medical Standard, including uncorrected visual acuity of 6/6 without glasses.

Key Preparation Strategy & Exam Day Guidelines

Success in RRB ALP CBT-1 requires balancing accuracy with speed. Candidates should focus heavily on core 10th-grade General Science concepts and high-frequency Reasoning topics. Daily timed practice tests are recommended to adapt to the 60-minute constraint for 75 questions.

On the day of the examination, candidates must report to their assigned test center well ahead of the gate closure time printed on their e-Admit Card. Essential items to carry include:

  • Printed copy of the official e-Admit Card downloaded from RRB portals.
  • Original, valid photo identification (Aadhaar Card, Passport, PAN Card, or Voter ID).
  • Recent colored passport-size photographs matching the one uploaded during online registration.

Step-by-Step Instructions

  1. Go to the official website of Railway Recruitment Boards at rrbcdg.gov.in.
  2. On the homepage, navigate to the 'Latest Notices' or 'Examination/Recruitment' section.
  3. Locate and select the link for 'RRB ALP 2026 Assistant Loco Pilot Computer Based Test (CBT-1) Exam Dates Announced'.
  4. Download and carefully review the official notice for verified instructions.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What is the official website to verify RRB ALP 2026 exam updates?

The official website for central RRB announcements is rrbcdg.gov.in. Candidates should verify all schedules directly on this portal.

Is there negative marking in the RRB ALP CBT-1 exam?

Yes, CBT-1 includes negative marking. One-third (1/3rd) of the mark allotted to a question is deducted for each incorrect answer.

Are B.E. or B.Tech degree holders eligible to apply for Assistant Loco Pilot?

Yes, candidates holding a Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics, or Automobile Engineering from a recognized university are eligible for the ALP post.

What medical vision standard is required for Assistant Loco Pilot selection?

Candidates must meet the A-1 Medical Standard. This includes distance vision of 6/6, 6/6 without glasses, near vision of 0.6, 0.6 without glasses, and passing tests for color vision, binocular vision, field of vision, and night vision.

Does CBT-1 score count towards the final merit list?

No, CBT-1 is purely a screening exam used to shortlist candidates for CBT-2. Final merit formulation depends on performance in CBT-2 Part A and the Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT).

What is the initial basic pay for an Assistant Loco Pilot under the 7th CPC?

The initial basic pay for an Assistant Loco Pilot is ₹19,900 per month under Pay Level 2 of the 7th CPC Pay Matrix, plus applicable allowances.

articles.content_html:
The Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB) officially published the Centralized Employment Notification for RRB NTPC 2026 on September 15, 2026, marking a major recruitment initiative for Indian civil service and railway job seekers. Covering 11,558 Graduate and Undergraduate Non-Technical Popular Categories positions, this notification provides structured career pathways across multiple administrative and operational cadres in Indian Railways. Aspirants are advised to access the official website at rrbcdg.gov.in to verify detailed eligibility rules, selection stages, and online submission procedures.

Key Highlights & Important Dates

Event / Activity Official Date / Status
Notification ReleasedSeptember 15, 2026
Online Application WindowCheck Official Portal
Last Date to ApplyRefer to Detailed Notification
Official Portalrrbcdg.gov.in

Recruitment & Eligibility Summary

Total VacanciesNot specified in the official notification.
Educational QualificationsRefer to the official notification guidelines.
Age Limit CriteriaAs per official rules specified in notification.
Application FeeCheck official notification for category-wise details.

Overview & Background of Railway Recruitment Boards Notification

The Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB) function under the Ministry of Railways to execute recruitment drives for technical and non-technical staff across all railway zones in India. The release of the Centralized Employment Notification (CEN) for Non-Technical Popular Categories (NTPC) 2026 stands as one of the significant recruitment notifications in the central government sector. Published on September 15, 2026, this notification addresses operational and administrative staffing needs across Indian Railways.

NTPC recruitment covers both undergraduate (10+2 standard) and graduate candidates. Post categories traditionally include roles such as Junior Clerk cum Typist, Accounts Clerk cum Typist, Trains Clerk, Commercial cum Ticket Clerk, Goods Guard, Senior Commercial cum Ticket Clerk, Station Master, and Commercial Apprentice. The centralized recruitment scheme ensures standardized evaluation criteria, unified computer-based examinations, and equitable merit formulation for candidates nationwide.

Eligibility Criteria & Minimum Educational Qualifications

Eligibility requirements for RRB NTPC 2026 are divided into two primary categories based on the entry pay level and responsibilities of the post. Applicants must hold qualifications from a recognized university or educational board before the final application closing date.

For Undergraduate Posts (Pay Level 2 and Level 3), candidates must have completed Class 12 (10+2 Stage) or its equivalent from a recognized Educational Board or Council. Candidates must meet the minimum aggregate marks required by the official guidelines, with standard score relaxations applicable to reserved categories.

For Graduate Posts (Pay Level 4, Level 5, and Level 6), applicants must hold a Bachelor's Degree in any discipline from a university incorporated by an Act of the Central or State Legislature in India or an equivalent institution recognized by the University Grants Commission (UGC). Candidates waiting for final degree results must have their final qualification declared on or before the deadline specified in the official notification.

Age Limit Criteria & Category-Wise Relaxations

Age thresholds for RRB NTPC positions are fixed as per standard central government recruitment rules, calculated as of the official cutoff date stated in the notification. The baseline age limit generally ranges between 18 to 30 years for undergraduate positions and 18 to 33 years for graduate posts.

Upper age relaxations are granted to candidates from reserved categories in compliance with Government of India orders. The general category-wise age relaxations are outlined below:

  • Other Backward Classes (OBC - Non-Creamy Layer): 3 Years upper age relaxation.
  • Scheduled Castes (SC) / Scheduled Tribes (ST): 5 Years upper age relaxation.
  • Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD): 10 Years for UR/EWS, 13 Years for OBC-NCL, and 15 Years for SC/ST.
  • Ex-Servicemen (ESM): Relaxation equal to defence service length plus 3 years, as per standing rules.

Pay Scale, Salary Structure & 7th CPC Allowances

Successful candidates are appointed across various Pay Levels of the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) Pay Matrix depending on the specific post grade. Alongside basic pay, appointees receive standard central government allowances and benefits.

Post LevelInitial Pay (7th CPC)Key Allowances Included
Level 2 (Undergraduate)₹19,900Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance (TA)
Level 3 (Undergraduate)₹21,700DA, HRA, TA, Running Allowance (for specific operational cadres)
Level 5 (Graduate)₹29,200DA, HRA, TA, Medical Benefits, National Pension System (NPS)
Level 6 (Graduate)₹35,400DA, HRA, TA, Pension Scheme, Railway Pass Privileges

Indian Railways employees also benefit from comprehensive healthcare under Railway Medical Facilities, duty-specific allowances, and subsidized railway pass concessions for self and dependents.

Comprehensive Examination Pattern & Syllabus Structure

The recruitment process utilizes a multi-stage Computer Based Test (CBT) structure designed to evaluate conceptual foundation, quantitative aptitude, and general awareness. Stage 1 CBT serves as a screening examination, whereas Stage 2 CBT scores determine core selection merit.

Stage 1 CBT consists of 100 objective multiple-choice questions with a total duration of 90 minutes. Stage 2 CBT includes 120 multiple-choice questions to be answered within 90 minutes. A negative marking penalty of 1/3rd mark applies for every incorrect response across both CBT stages.

Subject AreaStage 1 CBT QuestionsStage 2 CBT QuestionsCore Syllabus Topics
General Awareness4050Current Events, History, Indian Polity, Economy, Geography, General Science
Mathematics / Quantitative Aptitude3035Number Systems, Fractions, Ratio & Proportion, Percentage, Profit & Loss, Simple/Compound Interest
General Intelligence & Reasoning3035Analogies, Series, Coding-Decoding, Venn Diagrams, Syllogisms, Data Sufficiency

Step-by-Step Online Application & Document Upload Guide

Applicants must register and complete their forms online via the official recruitment portal at rrbcdg.gov.in. Applying to multiple RRBs for the same post group will result in the rejection of all applications.

  1. Official Portal Access: Navigate to rrbcdg.gov.in and click on the official CEN NTPC 2026 application link.
  2. Registration (OTR): Create a user profile using a valid email address and mobile number to obtain registration credentials.
  3. Application Form Entry: Enter personal details, academic qualifications, category classifications, and residential address accurately.
  4. Zone & Post Preference: Select preferred Railway Recruitment Board zones and rank post choices according to preference.
  5. Document Upload: Upload scanned copies of a clear passport photograph, signature, and category/community certificate (where applicable) meeting official file size requirements.
  6. Fee Payment & Final Submission: Pay the required application fee using online payment gateways. Verify all information before final submission and download a copy of the completed application form.

Selection Stages & Final Merit List Formulation

The selection pipeline involves sequential stages structured to assess candidates for administrative and technical responsibilities. Candidates must meet qualifying standards at each tier to advance in the recruitment cycle.

The complete process includes Stage 1 CBT (Screening), Stage 2 CBT (Merit Determination), Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT) or Typing Skill Test (for applicable posts like Station Master or Typist), Document Verification (DV), and a comprehensive Medical Examination conducted by Railway Medical Authorities.

Final merit lists are generated based on normalized scores secured in Stage 2 CBT (plus CBAT/Typing scores where applicable), subject to passing Document Verification and meeting the specific medical standards prescribed for each post cadre.

Key Preparation Strategy & Exam Day Guidelines

Preparing for RRB NTPC requires balancing speed and accuracy, particularly in Reasoning and Quantitative Aptitude. Practicing full-length mock tests and reviewing previous years' question papers aids in developing effective time allocation strategies for the 90-minute computer-based test.

On the day of the exam, candidates must carry a printed copy of the e-Call Letter (admit card), an original valid photo identity card (such as Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, PAN Card, or Passport), and recent passport-sized photographs. Electronic devices, smartwatches, calculators, and study notes are strictly forbidden inside the examination hall.

  1. Go to the official website of Railway Recruitment Boards at rrbcdg.gov.in.
  2. On the homepage, navigate to the 'Latest Notices' or 'Examination/Recruitment' section.
  3. Locate and select the link for 'RRB NTPC 2026 Centralized Employment Notification for 11,558 Graduate & Undergraduate Posts'.
  4. Download and carefully review the official notice for verified instructions.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What is the official website to verify the RRB NTPC 2026 notification details?

Candidates can verify all official updates, download notices, and submit applications directly on the official portal at rrbcdg.gov.in.

Are final-year students eligible to apply for Graduate NTPC posts?

Generally, candidates must possess their final degree qualification and marksheets on or before the official closing date for applications specified in the detailed notification.

What age relaxation is provided for OBC and SC/ST candidates?

In accordance with central government rules, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates receive a 3-year upper age relaxation, while SC and ST candidates receive a 5-year upper age relaxation.

Is there negative marking in the RRB NTPC Computer Based Tests?

Yes, a negative marking deduction of 1/3rd (0.33) mark is applied for every incorrect response in both Stage 1 and Stage 2 CBTs.

How is the final merit list calculated for NTPC posts?

The final merit list is compiled using normalized marks from Stage 2 CBT (and qualifying scores in CBAT/Typing tests where applicable), subject to clearing Document Verification and the prescribed Medical Fitness Test.

articles.content_html:
The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) published the official answer key and minimum qualifying cutoff marks for the National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination (II) 2026 on September 15, 2026. Candidates who appeared for the nationwide competitive exam can now download the master keys across all test sets to calculate their official raw scores. The disclosure of set-wise answer keys and subject-wise qualifying benchmarks ensures complete transparency in the written selection process.

Key Highlights & Important Dates

Event / Activity Official Date / Status
Notification ReleasedSeptember 15, 2026
Result Declaration DateSeptember 15, 2026 (Declared)
Scorecard Download WindowAvailable on Official Portal
Official Portalupsc.gov.in

Overview & Background of Union Public Service Commission Notification

The Union Public Service Commission conducts the National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination twice a year to recruit eligible candidates for training at the National Defence Academy (NDA), Khadakwasla, and the Indian Naval Academy (INA), Ezhimala. On September 15, 2026, the commission officially published the verified answer key along with the minimum cutoff marks for the NDA & NA (II) 2026 written examination.

Aspirants can access the official notification document directly via upsc.gov.in to evaluate their performance. Reviewing the master key helps candidates verify their marked options against the commission's official evaluation standard. This milestone allows candidates preparing for subsequent selection stages to gauge competitive thresholds accurately across both Mathematics and General Ability Test papers.

Eligibility Criteria & Minimum Educational Qualifications

Educational qualifications for the NDA & NA examination vary according to the defense wing selected during the application process. For the Army Wing of the National Defence Academy, candidates must have passed the 12th Class examination under the 10+2 pattern of school education or an equivalent examination conducted by a recognized State Education Board or University.

For the Air Force and Naval Wings of the National Defence Academy, as well as for the 10+2 Cadet Entry Scheme at the Indian Naval Academy, candidates must have passed the 12th Class examination with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics as compulsory subjects. Candidates currently appearing in the 12th Class under the 10+2 pattern are also eligible to apply, provided they submit proof of passing by the deadline specified in the official notification guidelines.

Age Limit Criteria & Category-Wise Relaxations

The Union Public Service Commission enforces strict age criteria for entry into the Armed Forces through the National Defence Academy. Only unmarried male and female candidates born within the specific date bracket outlined in the official notification are eligible to apply. Generally, candidates must be aged between 16.5 and 19.5 years at the commencement of the training course.

Unlike civil service examinations, defense entry examinations like NDA & NA do not offer upper age relaxations to candidates belonging to reserved categories such as SC, ST, or OBC. This uniform age limit ensures that candidates join the officer training academies within the prescribed physical and operational parameters established by the Ministry of Defence.

Pay Scale, Salary Structure & 7th CPC Allowances

Selected candidates undergo rigorous pre-commission training at the National Defence Academy and respective service academies. During the cadet training period, trainees receive a fixed stipend of Rs. 56,100 per month, which corresponds to Pay Level 10 of the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) matrix.

Upon successful commissioning as a Lieutenant in the Army or equivalent ranks in the Navy and Air Force, officers enter Pay Level 10 (Rs. 56,100 to Rs. 1,77,500). In addition to basic pay, officers receive Military Service Pay (MSP) of Rs. 15,500 per month, Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance, and specialized operational allowances such as Flying Allowance or Submarine Allowance wherever applicable.

Comprehensive Examination Pattern & Syllabus Structure

The UPSC NDA & NA written examination consists of two objective-type papers totaling 900 marks. Paper I focuses on Mathematics (300 marks) spanning 120 questions over a duration of 2.5 hours. Paper II is the General Ability Test (GAT) carrying 600 marks with 150 questions over 2.5 hours, split into Part A (English - 200 marks) and Part B (General Knowledge - 400 marks).

Part B of the GAT paper covers Physics, Chemistry, General Science, History, Freedom Movement, Geography, and Current Events. A penalty of one-third (0.33) of the marks assigned to a question is deducted for every incorrect response. Candidates must score minimum qualifying marks in each individual paper—typically 25%—in addition to securing the overall aggregate cutoff score.

Step-by-Step Online Application & Document Upload Guide

While the present release focuses on the official answer key and cutoff disclosure, candidates interacting with the UPSC online portal for ongoing or future recruitments must follow the commission's standardized One Time Registration (OTR) procedure on upsc.gov.in. Below are the steps to access the current official answer key document:

  1. Go to the official website of the Union Public Service Commission at upsc.gov.in.
  2. On the homepage, navigate to the 'Latest Notices' or 'Examination/Recruitment' section.
  3. Locate and select the link titled 'UPSC NDA & NA (II) 2026 Official Answer Key and Cutoff Marks Out'.
  4. Download the PDF document (nda-2-2026-answer-key.pdf) to review set-wise keys and verified evaluation guidelines.

Selection Stages & Final Merit List Formulation

The recruitment process for the National Defence Academy comprises two main stages: the written examination conducted by UPSC and the Services Selection Board (SSB) interview. Candidates who clear the written cutoff threshold receive invitations for the 5-day SSB selection process, which evaluates intelligence and personality traits.

The SSB stage includes Stage I (Officer Intelligence Rating tests and Picture Perception & Description Test) and Stage II (Psychological Tests, Group Testing Officer Tasks, Personal Interview, and Conference). The final merit list is compiled by aggregating the marks obtained in the written exam (900 marks) and the SSB interview (900 marks), totaling 1800 marks, subject to medical fitness clearance.

Key Preparation Strategy & Exam Day Guidelines

Aspirants aiming for future NDA examinations must build strong fundamentals in 11th and 12th-grade Mathematics, particularly Algebra, Trigonometry, Analytical Geometry, Differential Calculus, and Statistics. Solving previous year question papers using official UPSC answer keys offers authentic insights into question trends and marking standards.

For the General Ability Test, regular reading of national newspapers enhances English vocabulary and current affairs awareness. On examination day, candidates must bring a printed admit card, valid photo identity proof, and a black ballpoint pen for marking the OMR sheet. Maintaining accuracy is essential to minimize negative marking penalties.

Step-by-Step Instructions

  1. Go to the official website of Union Public Service Commission at upsc.gov.in.
  2. On the homepage, navigate to the 'Latest Notices' or 'Examination/Recruitment' section.
  3. Locate and select the link for 'UPSC NDA & NA (II) 2026 Official Answer Key and Cutoff Marks Out'.
  4. Download and carefully review the official notice for verified instructions.

Verified Direct Links

Official Website (upsc.gov.in)Visit Official Portal ↗

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What is the official website to verify this Union Public Service Commission update?

The official website is upsc.gov.in. Candidates are strictly advised to rely on official links to access notifications and answer keys.

Where can candidates download the official notification and answer key PDF?

Candidates can download the official document directly from upsc.gov.in/notices/nda-2-2026-answer-key.pdf or via the examination section on upsc.gov.in.

What is the negative marking policy for the UPSC NDA written exam?

There is a negative marking of one-third (0.33) of the total marks assigned to a question for every incorrect answer marked on the OMR sheet.

Are candidates appearing in Class 12 eligible for the NDA & NA exam?

Yes, candidates appearing in the 12th Class under the 10+2 pattern are eligible to apply, subject to producing proof of passing by the deadline given in the notification.

What is the total mark weightage for the NDA & NA selection process?

The selection process totals 1800 marks, comprising 900 marks for the written examination and 900 marks for the SSB interview.

Is there an upper age relaxation for SC/ST or OBC candidates in NDA recruitment?

No, age limits for the NDA & NA examination are uniform across all categories, and no upper age relaxation is granted to reserved category applicants.

articles.content_html:
The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) has officially published the e-Admit Card notice for the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026 on September 15, 2026. Candidates who successfully cleared the preliminary stage can now download their hall tickets directly through the official portal at upsc.gov.in. Applicants must verify all personal credentials and exam center instructions on the official document prior to attending the descriptive examination sessions.

Key Highlights & Important Dates

Event / Activity Official Date / Status
Notification ReleasedSeptember 15, 2026
Admit Card Release DateSeptember 15, 2026 (Out Now)
Exam DateRefer to Official Schedule
Official Portalupsc.gov.in

Overview & Background of Union Public Service Commission Notification

The Union Public Service Commission administers India's premier civil services recruitment framework to select administrative, diplomatic, police, and financial service personnel. Following the evaluation of the preliminary screening test, qualified candidates progress to the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026. The release of the e-Admit Card on September 15, 2026, marks the final administrative step leading to the written descriptive stage across designated national examination centers.

Candidates must secure a printed copy of the e-Admit Card well before the exam date. The hall ticket serves as an essential entry permit and carries key information including roll numbers, venue details, exam timings, and candidate identification data. Retaining a clean printout throughout the examination process remains mandatory for all candidates across India.

Eligibility Criteria & Minimum Educational Qualifications

Eligibility for the Civil Services Examination requires candidates to hold a bachelor's degree from a university incorporated by an Act of the Central or State Legislature in India. Qualifications obtained through educational institutions established by an Act of Parliament or declared to be deemed as a University under Section 3 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, are fully valid. Candidates possessing equivalent qualifications recognized by the central government are also considered eligible.

Candidates who have appeared at an examination the passing of which would render them educationally qualified for the Commission's examination, but have not been informed of the result, were permitted provisionally to apply for the preliminary stage. However, for entry to the Main examination stage, candidates must present proof of passing the requisite qualifying university examination along with their Detailed Application Form (DAF).

Age Limit Criteria & Category-Wise Relaxations

The baseline age limit for candidates applying for civil service positions strictly mandates a minimum age of 21 years and a maximum age ceiling of 32 years as calculated on the official cut-off date published in the primary notification. Relaxation in upper age limits is extended to specific reserved categories in accordance with central government regulations:

  • Other Backward Classes (OBC): Upper age relaxation of up to 3 years (maximum age ceiling 35 years).
  • Scheduled Castes / Scheduled Tribes (SC/ST): Upper age relaxation of up to 5 years (maximum age ceiling 37 years).
  • Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD): Upper age relaxation of up to 10 years across qualifying functional categories.
  • Ex-Servicemen & Defense Personnel: Relaxation provided as per designated statutory norms based on continuous military service history.

Pay Scale, Salary Structure & 7th CPC Allowances

Recruits selected through the UPSC Civil Services Examination enter administrative cadres at Pay Level 10 of the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) Pay Matrix. The initial basic pay for entry-level appointments (such as Junior Time Scale officers in IAS, IPS, IFS, and IRS) stands at ₹56,100 per month.

In addition to the base salary, selected officers receive standard central government allowances including Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA) categorized by city classification (X, Y, Z cities ranging from 9% to 27%), Transport Allowance (TA), comprehensive medical care under CGHS, and defined pension cover. Career progression offers structured promotions leading to higher administrative pay scales up to Cabinet Secretary level (Pay Level 17).

Comprehensive Examination Pattern & Syllabus Structure

The Civil Services (Main) Examination consists of a written descriptive examination comprising 9 distinct papers, followed by a Personality Test (Interview). Out of the 9 written papers, 2 are qualifying language papers while the remaining 7 count towards the final merit order.

Paper CategorySubject DetailsTotal MarksQualifying / Merit
Paper AOne Indian Language (from 8th Schedule)300 MarksQualifying (25% Minimum)
Paper BEnglish Language300 MarksQualifying (25% Minimum)
Paper IEssay Writing250 MarksMerit Ranking
Paper IIGeneral Studies I (Indian Heritage, History, Geography, Society)250 MarksMerit Ranking
Paper IIIGeneral Studies II (Governance, Constitution, Polity, Social Justice, IR)250 MarksMerit Ranking
Paper IVGeneral Studies III (Technology, Economic Dev, Environment, Security)250 MarksMerit Ranking
Paper VGeneral Studies V (Ethics, Integrity, and Aptitude)250 MarksMerit Ranking
Paper VIOptional Subject - Paper 1250 MarksMerit Ranking
Paper VIIOptional Subject - Paper 2250 MarksMerit Ranking

Written papers are descriptive in nature, demanding structured, concise, and analytical answers. The total score for the written Main examination stands at 1,750 marks. Candidates who achieve qualifying marks above the cut-off threshold proceed to the final Personality Test stage.

Step-by-Step Online Application & Document Download Guide

Candidates eligible to download the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026 e-Admit Card should follow the verified step-by-step instructions detailed below:

  1. Visit the official portal of the Union Public Service Commission at upsc.gov.in.
  2. Locate the 'Latest Notices' or 'e-Admit Cards' tab featured prominently on the homepage.
  3. Click on the direct link titled 'UPSC Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026 e-Admit Card Released'.
  4. Input your assigned Registration ID or Roll Number along with your registered Date of Birth.
  5. Review the details displayed on screen, verify personal identification data, and click 'Download'.
  6. Save the PDF file securely and generate multiple printed hard copies on clean A4 paper sheets.

Selection Stages & Final Merit List Formulation

The comprehensive selection procedure for recruitment through the UPSC Civil Services Examination involves three successive stages:

  • Stage 1: Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination — Objective screening test comprising GS Paper I and CSAT Paper II (Qualifying).
  • Stage 2: Civil Services (Main) Examination — Descriptive written examination of 9 papers totaling 1,750 marks for merit ranking.
  • Stage 3: Personality Test (Interview) — Oral assessment carrying 275 marks to evaluate candidate suitability for administrative responsibilities.

The final merit list is compiled strictly on the basis of aggregate marks secured by candidates in the Main Written Examination (1,750 marks) and the Personality Test (275 marks), resulting in a cumulative score evaluated out of 2,025 marks. Allocation to services (IAS, IPS, IFS, Group A/B) depends on final rank, service preference, category status, and verified medical fitness.

Key Preparation Strategy & Exam Day Guidelines

Candidates appearing for the descriptive written examination must ensure strict adherence to operational guidelines. Candidates must carry a clear printed copy of the e-Admit Card along with an official government photo identity proof (e.g., Aadhaar Card, Passport, Voter ID, Driving License) whose number matches the one recorded in the Detailed Application Form.

Exam day rules require candidates to arrive at the allotted venue at least 30 minutes prior to the scheduled session commencement time. Mobile phones, smartwatches, Bluetooth gadgets, programmable calculators, and unauthorized paper materials are strictly banned inside examination premises. Standard blue or black ballpoint pens must be used for completing answer booklets according to commission guidelines.

Step-by-Step Instructions

  1. Go to the official website of Union Public Service Commission at upsc.gov.in.
  2. On the homepage, navigate to the 'Latest Notices' or 'Examination/Recruitment' section.
  3. Locate and select the link for 'UPSC Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026 e-Admit Card Released'.
  4. Download and carefully review the official notice for verified instructions.

Verified Direct Links

Resource / Document Direct Official Link
Official Notification PDFClick Here ↗
Official Website (upsc.gov.in)Visit Official Portal ↗

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What is the official website to verify and download the UPSC Main Admit Card 2026?

The official website for verifying UPSC notices and downloading hall tickets is upsc.gov.in. Candidates should strictly avoid unverified third-party portals.

When was the UPSC Civil Services (Main) 2026 e-Admit Card released?

The e-Admit Card notice was officially released by the Union Public Service Commission on September 15, 2026.

Are marks obtained in Paper A and Paper B counted in the final merit list?

No. Paper A (Indian Language) and Paper B (English) are qualifying papers carrying 300 marks each. Candidates must secure minimum qualifying percentage marks (25%), but these marks are not added to the final merit score.

What should I do if there is a discrepancy on my UPSC e-Admit Card?

In case of any discrepancy in personal details, photograph, signature, or exam venue on the e-Admit Card, candidates should immediately contact the Union Public Service Commission via their official helpdesk or email specified on upsc.gov.in.

What is the total marks scheme for the UPSC Civil Services Main Written and Interview stages?

The written descriptive examination accounts for 1,750 marks across 7 merit papers, while the Personality Test carries 275 marks. The final merit list is formulated out of a total of 2,025 marks.

What documents must be carried to the examination center alongside the e-Admit Card?

Candidates must carry a clear printed copy of the downloaded e-Admit Card along with the original photo identity card specified in their application (such as Aadhaar Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving License).
